provider: Open Context (archaeology / cultural heritage data publisher)

free_tier.stated: No published byte cap. 'Essentially, we provide publication services for the vast bulk of media that typically cannot fit into a conventional book or article publication.' Volume is negotiated with editors, not metered.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Free and open: content is published under CC-BY or CC0 with no paywall and no metering, and is archived with leading digital libraries.

tooling: Read side is a real API plus OAI-PMH and DOI resolution; the WRITE side is deliberately not programmatic. 'The first step is to contact the Open Context editorial team.. we think it's important to start with a personal contact rather than an impersonal upload button.' No upload endpoint.
chaining: Unlimited projects, but each is editorially co-produced, so throughput is bounded by the editorial team, not by quota.
limits_note: No self-serve upload at all; structured data (spreadsheets/relational) plus media only; PDFs generally excluded unless documenting a dataset; editorial vetting with orange-dot status levels before release.

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

reliability_note: Genuinely open door ('Anyone can publish their research with Open Context — from individuals to teams') but human-in-the-loop by design, so it is an archive of last resort, not storage.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.
